reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: None for the request itself. However, one assumption in the reading is factually wrong: 'the reader prompt has only 3 tokens of headroom; any briefs.rs edit must not grow the reader prompt'. READING_RULES is in the reader brief, which is outside BudgetSet::Reader (lib.rs:279-283). The plan built Decision 3 on that wrong premise. (round 1 of 3). The plan fixes the cause in the right place. It adds a deterministic `check_design_existing_code` step to `refusing_check`, next to `check_code_survey`, and the corpus guard makes it ship with a refusing case. What I read in the snapshot matches what the plan names: `refusing_check` and `check_code_survey` (reading.rs:3042 and 3375), `code_surveys` and `names_crates_path`, `"design"` as a class (routing.rs:50), and in the corpus `base_reading`, `repo_files` (which includes docs/design/roadmap.md and crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs), `INPUT_FORMS: [&str; 15]` and `code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended`. The demonstrations run the real gate and the corpus with no test doubles, and each would fail without the change. One design decision is wrong, and the reading shares the mistake. Decision 3 teaches the rule only through the refusal message and justifies this by the reader token budget and the 5-line assertion. Neither applies. `BudgetSet::Reader` covers only CONTRACT, READER_FRAME, defaults and catalog (athena-context/src/lib.rs:279-283). READING_RULES and CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE are in the reader brief, outside that budget. The line-count test compares against `READING_RULES.len()`, so it does not pin the count at 5. As planned, the reader is never told the rule before it writes, so nearly every design reading is refused on its first read and uses up the one second read that briefs.rs:1692-1693 describes. The existing rule that each check has a reader rule line (briefs.rs:3400-3409) is also bypassed. Smaller weaknesses: the criterion match accepts any criterion containing the words 'existing code' and 'section', and the assumption can name the doc the job is about to create as its "existing" path. Findings: major: The rule is taught only by refusing the reading, based on a token budget that does not cover the reading rules. Every design reading is likely to be refused once. (Plan Decision 3, step 5, and the reading's assumption 'the reader prompt has only 3 tokens of headroom'; crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:279-283, crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:1692-1700 and 3389-3412); minor: The criterion match accepts any criterion that contains the words 'existing code' and 'section' anywhere, including ones that say the opposite. (Plan Decision 2 and step 1 (`names_existing_code_section`)); minor: An `Existing code:` assumption can pass by naming only the doc the job is creating, so no existing code is actually named. (Plan Decision 2 and step 2 (assumption path test)); nit: The intended-refusal test reads the doc comment with the same split pattern as the existing test. That works, but it makes the new test depend on the function being declared exactly as `pub fn check_design_existing_code`. (Plan Criterion 4 demonstration)
